description: Every token is built from exactly one primitive: a translucent, axis-rotated filled square, scattered across a near-black warm charcoal ground with no strokes, lines, curves, glyphs or any second shape anywhere in the twelve. The palette is a tight warm earth range — near-black brown, mid taupe/khaki, and a burnt-orange terracotta accent — and because the quads are semi-transparent, overlaps accumulate into lighter, soft-edged patches, so dense seeds read as a single agglomerated mass while the individual squares dissolve. Structure is consistently 'central clump plus outlying debris': a cluster near the middle of the frame with satellite squares thrown outward, and the frame itself is used only as passive surrounding negative space — no border, no ground line, no edge-anchored composition — though a couple of seeds (9727, 10443) run their outermost squares into and slightly past the frame edge. What the twelve share is the primitive, the palette, the dark ground, the translucent accumulation and the clump-plus-scatter logic; what varies is element count (roughly 8 to 60+), element scale, spread and silhouette — 9011 and 10801 are sparse handfuls of large isolated squares, 9369 / 10264 / 9727 are dense brown masses filling most of the frame, 9906 is a diffuse annular field of tiny fragments, 10443 is a horizontal band and 10622 a short diagonal chain. Across the three market conditions the ONLY thing that changes is uniform scale: every element dilates about a common center, with identical count, identical positions, identical rotations, identical hues and identical layering — neutral is smallest, stress largest, recovery intermediate and visibly closer to stress than to neutral. There is no colour shift, no re-composition, no appearance or disappearance of elements, and no change in the object's topology; the pieces simply breathe in and out.
seenAt120: At browse size the primitive and the palette survive completely — warm brown-and-orange squares on black is legible instantly — and so does the gross density class: sparse handful vs. dense mass vs. diffuse dust vs. band. What is lost is all internal structure of the dense seeds: 9369, 10264, 9727 and 9548 collapse into an amorphous soft brown blob with orange confetti around its rim, individual square boundaries gone. The orange accents are the only real colour signal that carries. Twelve distinct tokens do not fully survive: they resolve into about four recognisable types, and within a type they are hard to tell apart — 9011 and 10801 both read as 'a few orange squares floating on black', 9369 and 10264 both as 'brown blob'. Silhouette differences between those pairs are real but slight at this size. A ~25-35% uniform scale change is perceptible on the sparse seeds at 120px and marginal on the dense ones, where growth mostly just thickens an already-saturated mass.
